_comment: The ONLY Alpaca tools the language model is ever shown. This file is the enforcement point for the architecture in PLAN.md section 1 and is asserted by tests/test_tool_mediation.py.
_why_a_code_allowlist: ALPACA_TOOLSETS scoping exists but cannot express this split. The 'trading' toolset bundles get_all_positions / get_open_position / get_orders -- which the agent genuinely needs -- with place_option_order, close_position, close_all_positions, cancel_all_orders and five more write tools. There is no value of that variable that yields position reads without also yielding order placement. See docs/mcp_tools.md section 3.
_allowlist_by_inclusion: Named individually rather than derived by subtracting known write tools from the enabled toolsets. Stage 1 found four tools -- get_locates, get_locate, get_locate_quotes and the WRITE tool create_locate -- that belong to no documented toolset at all. A subtractive allowlist would have missed create_locate entirely.
_write_tools_comment: Never passed to the model. The ORCHESTRATOR calls place_option_order on gate approval and close_position for exits, through MCPClient.call_write() -- a separate method the model has no route to. Listed here so the safety test can assert on the complete set rather than a remembered subset; enumerated live from the server in Stage 1.
_toolsets_note: Defence in depth only -- it removes watchlists, crypto, news, fixed-income, index and locates from the process entirely (74 tools down to 38). The allowlist above remains the enforcement point, because it is the thing under test.
_model_tools_comment: The subset of read_tools actually handed to the MODEL. Smaller than read_tools on purpose: every schema is resent on every turn, and the full eleven cost ~3,900 tokens per request -- half of Groq's free-tier 8,000 tokens-per-minute budget, which made requests larger than the entire per-minute allowance. The tools left out are ones the ORCHESTRATOR calls deterministically and the analyst has no use for: bars feed IV rank (already given in the preamble), get_orders drives idempotency, and get_option_contracts / get_stock_snapshot / get_open_position are covered by the chain, latest trade, and get_all_positions respectively. Narrowing this list also narrows what the model can reach, so it is a security improvement as well as a budget one.
